claim: Photinus carolinus fireflies flash with no intrinsic period between successive bursts when in isolation from their peers.
source: In isolation from their peers, Photinus carolinus fireflies flash with no intrinsic period between successive bursts.
evidence: This is stated as an observed characteristic of isolated P. carolinus fireflies in the abstract.

claim: Photinus carolinus fireflies transition into predictability and synchronize with their neighbors with rhythmic periodicity when congregating into large mating swarms.
source: Yet, when congregating into large mating swarms, these fireflies transition into predictability, synchronizing with their neighbors with a rhythmic periodicity.
evidence: This is stated as an observed behavior of P. carolinus fireflies in swarms in the abstract.

claim: A mechanism for emergence of synchrony and periodicity in P. carolinus fireflies can be formulated in a mathematical framework.
source: Here we propose a mechanism for emergence of synchrony and periodicity, and formulate the principle in a mathematical framework.
evidence: The authors state they have developed a mathematical framework for the observed phenomenon.

claim: Analytic predictions from the proposed mathematical framework agree strikingly well with data without using fitting parameters.
source: Remarkably, with no fitting parameters, analytic predictions from this simple principle and framework agree strikingly well with data.
evidence: The authors claim their analytical model predictions match experimental data without parameter fitting.

claim: An agent-based computational framework featuring groups of random oscillators via integrate-and-fire interactions controlled by a tunable parameter can model P. carolinus firefly interactions.
source: Next, we add further sophistication to the framework using a computational approach featuring groups of random oscillators via integrate-and-fire interactions controlled by a tunable parameter.
evidence: The authors describe their computational modeling approach.

claim: The agent-based framework of P. carolinus fireflies interacting in swarms of increasing density shows quantitatively similar phenomenology to the observed behavior.
source: This agent-based framework of P. carolinus fireflies interacting in swarms of increasing density also shows quantitatively similar phenomenology and reduces to the analytic framework in the appropriate limit of the tunable coupling strength.
evidence: The authors state their computational model reproduces the observed phenomena quantitatively.

claim: The agent-based framework reduces to the analytic framework in the appropriate limit of the tunable coupling strength.
source: This agent-based framework of P. carolinus fireflies interacting in swarms of increasing density also shows quantitatively similar phenomenology and reduces to the analytic framework in the appropriate limit of the tunable coupling strength.
evidence: The authors state that their computational model converges to their analytical model under specific parameter conditions.

claim: The resulting dynamics of P. carolinus firefly synchronization follow the style of a decentralized follow-the-leader synchronization.
source: We discuss our findings and note that the resulting dynamics follow the style of a decentralized follow-the-leader synchronization, where any of the randomly flashing individuals may take the role of the leader of any subsequent synchronized flash burst.
evidence: The authors characterize the synchronization mechanism as decentralized follow-the-leader based on their findings.

claim: Any randomly flashing individual P. carolinus firefly may take the role of the leader of any subsequent synchronized flash burst.
source: We discuss our findings and note that the resulting dynamics follow the style of a decentralized follow-the-leader synchronization, where any of the randomly flashing individuals may take the role of the leader of any subsequent synchronized flash burst.
evidence: The authors describe the leadership role in synchronization as non-fixed and potentially assumed by any individual.

claim: Synchrony and periodicity in P. carolinus fireflies are emergent properties that arise from collective behavior.
source: In isolation from their peers, Photinus carolinus fireflies flash with no intrinsic period between successive bursts. Yet, when congregating into large mating swarms, these fireflies transition into predictability, synchronizing with their neighbors with a rhythmic periodicity.
evidence: The contrast between isolated and collective behavior implies that synchrony and periodicity emerge from group interactions rather than being intrinsic properties.

claim: Firefly density affects the synchronization behavior in P. carolinus swarms.
source: This agent-based framework of P. carolinus fireflies interacting in swarms of increasing density also shows quantitatively similar phenomenology and reduces to the analytic framework in the appropriate limit of the tunable coupling strength.
evidence: The mention of 'swarms of increasing density' as a variable in the model implies that density is a factor affecting synchronization.

claim: The synchronization of P. carolinus fireflies occurs in the context of mating behavior.
source: Yet, when congregating into large mating swarms, these fireflies transition into predictability, synchronizing with their neighbors with a rhythmic periodicity.
evidence: The text explicitly states that the swarms where synchronization occurs are mating swarms.
